brief.analysis: The strongest regime argument is a genuine multi-year rearmament cycle — NATO on a path toward 5% of GDP and record 2026 procurement — which structurally lifts defense's share of the market and invalidates a flat 5-year mean for ITA/SPY. This is corroborated by the data itself: raw_and_detrended_diverge is true (raw z 1.73 vs detrended 0.70), direct evidence the underlying mean is drifting upward, so the ratio is barely stretched against its own trend. With ma_score 0/3 and the 200DMA target essentially already met (+0.5%), there is no clean reversion left to harvest.
brief.report_line: Avoid short ITA/SPY — the detrended z (0.70 vs raw 1.73) confirms the mean is drifting up on a structural defense-spending regime, leaving no reversion edge to the 200DMA.

brief.analysis: The regime case is decisive: the gold/silver ratio already round-tripped from >100:1 to ~57:1 with silver up ~147% in 2025 on solar/electronics demand, so silver's relative strength (a rising SLV/GLD) is structural, not a dislocation to fade. The 200DMA target is already ACHIEVED and current z has collapsed to 1.06 from a peak of 6.36 — the edge is gone, and the remaining +14.7% to the 5y mean asks silver to underperform gold into a live industrial-demand tailwind. The old 5-year mean formed before the silver deficit/solar regime and is an invalid target despite the HIGH CONVICTION flag.
brief.report_line: Do not add to short SLV/GLD — the mean-reversion is essentially complete (200DMA achieved, z back to ~1) and the residual push to the 5-year mean fights a structural silver-demand regime.

brief.analysis: The regime case is strong: copper and industrial metals are in a structurally tight, deficit-driven upcycle powered by electrification, energy transition and the AI-datacenter buildout, so XME's relative strength reflects a demand regime rather than a fadeable spike. The trade is already exhausted — 200DMA target ACHIEVED, current z just 0.69 (peak 4.57), detrended z -0.08 — meaning the ratio sits essentially on its own trend, with the remaining +11.3% to the 5y mean asking metals to underperform into that tailwind. The 5-year mean predates the current commodity regime and is not a valid target despite the HIGH CONVICTION flag.
brief.report_line: Avoid short XME/SPY — reversion is spent (200DMA achieved, z ~0.7, detrended ~0) and the push to the 5-year mean bets against a structural metals/copper deficit upcycle.

brief.analysis: The strongest regime argument is that the AI capex cycle is still expanding into 2026, with semis now roughly 20% of developed-market equity, so SMH's premium over QQQ reflects a persistent secular bid rather than a temporary stretch. The 5y-mean target (0.4719, +73.8%) is almost certainly an invalid anchor because that mean predates the AI capex regime; only the 200DMA target (+19.4%) is a defensible reversion. Raw and detrended z agree (3.0 vs 2.89) so the mean is not obviously drifting on this window, but a 5-year lookback spanning the pre-AI era understates the structural rerating, and the base rate (6/8 to the 200DMA) only ever validated the moving-average target, not the mean.
brief.report_line: Short SMH/QQQ toward the 200DMA (+19.4%) only, sized down — the 5-year mean is a pre-AI-capex anchor that likely no longer applies, so the reversion target is the moving average, not the mean.
